cleanApp.headline: Your app doesn't know we exist.

telescopeCallout.quote: Telescope works inside your app. Buggregator works beside it.
telescopeCallout.body: Zero performance overhead. Works with RoadRunner, FrankenPHP, Swoole, and Octane. Catches emails, SMS, and external HTTP — things Telescope never sees. Works across every service in your stack.

cleanApp.body: Buggregator runs beside your application — as one binary or one Docker container. Your codebase doesn't change. Your dependencies don't change. You already have the SDKs installed — they just need a different address.

noDeps.title: No new dependencies
noDeps.body: Your app's composer.json stays untouched. No service providers. No migrations. No Buggregator code inside your project.

oneEnvVar.title: One env variable
oneEnvVar.body: Already using Sentry SDK, VarDumper, or Monolog? Change where they send data. That's it. Your code doesn't need to know about Buggregator.

crossProject.title: One instance, all your apps
crossProject.body: Run one Buggregator — binary or container. Point all your projects at it. Microservices, monorepos, multiple teams — one dashboard.

devEnv.headline: Made for dev environments.
devEnv.subheadline: No account. No credit card. No project setup.
devEnv.body: Add Buggregator to your docker-compose.yml alongside your other services. Change your .env. Start debugging. That's 60 seconds — not 15 minutes of cloud dashboard configuration.

showcase.title: Everything in one dashboard
showcase.subtitle: 12 debugging tools. One interface.

descriptions.exceptions: Catch unhandled exceptions with full stack traces via Sentry SDK. See exactly where your code breaks.
descriptions.profiler: Visualize XHProf call graphs to find performance bottlenecks. Click any node to trace the path from entry point.
descriptions.vardump: Inspect variables with dump(). See object properties, array contents, and types — right in the browser.
descriptions.ray: Debug with ray() — tables, queries, models, jobs, mail, counters and 18 more payload types. Works with PHP, JS, Ruby, Go SDKs.
descriptions.emails: Intercept outgoing emails during development. Preview HTML, inspect headers — no emails actually sent.
descriptions.logs: Aggregate Monolog, Symfony, and Laravel logs in real time. Search by message, channel or level.
descriptions.http: Capture and inspect incoming HTTP requests. See headers, body, and query parameters at a glance.
descriptions.httpProxy: See every HTTP request your app makes to external APIs — with full response. Set HTTP_PROXY and capture Guzzle, cURL, and SDK calls. Replaces Charles, Fiddler, and mitmproxy.
descriptions.inspector: Monitor application performance with transaction tracing, memory tracking, and timeline breakdowns. Local APM alternative.
descriptions.sms: Intercept outgoing SMS during development. Auto-detects 40+ providers including Twilio, Vonage, Plivo, Sinch, and more.
descriptions.mockServer: Fake the API your app depends on. Set a rule — method, path, status, headers, body, delay — and /mock answers with it. Every call is captured, with the rule that answered or why none matched.
descriptions.xdebug: See a paused Xdebug session in the browser: stack, variables, source, and watches when eval is on. Stepping stays in your IDE, which gets the session unchanged; your AI assistant can read it over MCP. Off by default.

trap.title: Debugging functions for your PHP code
trap.description: A Composer package with trap(), tr() and td() — drop-in replacements for dump() and dd(). Chain .depth(), .once(), .if() to dump only what you need. Call tr() between two lines to see the time and memory spent. Works on its own or with the full server.

jetbrains.title: Never leave your IDE
jetbrains.description: The Buggregator plugin for PhpStorm brings dumps, logs, and debug data directly into your editor.

testo.title: Tests without the boilerplate
testo.description: Testo is a PHP testing framework. Write tests as classes, plain functions or attributes right on your code — no TestCase to extend. Assertions grouped by type, benchmarks with one {attr} attribute, and a PhpStorm plugin. PHP 8.2+, now in open beta.

mock.title: Fake the API you're waiting for
mock.desc: The API isn't ready, or its sandbox is slow? Write a rule — method, path, status, body, delay — and Buggregator answers /mock/... with it. Every call is recorded, with what was sent back or why no rule matched. Rules can live in buggregator.yaml, so CI gets the same answers.

ai.title: Let your AI assistant see the runtime
ai.desc: Your AI assistant can read your code but not what happened when it ran. Buggregator's MCP server lets Claude Code, Cursor and other MCP clients read your errors, dumps and profiles. With the new Xdebug proxy, they can also read a paused session — stack and variables — while your IDE stays in control. Off by default. The Xdebug tools read the paused session; stepping stays in your IDE.
